To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social and institutional indicators are needed for wildlife and fish management, that these indicators are not well developed at the present time, and that a model for their development is available in the field of social indicators.

the social and institutional dimensions of the wildlife and fishery management process are in need of explicit attention and that a comprehensive system of social and institutional indicators is available to help resource managers improve all phases of the process, from goal setting and objective setting to evaluation.
a system of social and institutional indicators can provide an important tool for improving wildlife and fishery management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a set of social and institutional indicators for wildlife and fisheries management.
the social dimensions of resource management and with the institutional arrangements for resource management, including the role and function of government agencies.
the human dimension of wildlife and fish resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the indicator system is a potentially useful tool for wildlife and fishy resource managers and researchers.
the system of social and institutional indicators presented here is useful for improving all phases and components of wildlife and fish and wildlife management.
the social and institutional performance indicators are a useful and necessary component of any wildlife and fishery management system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for wildlife and fishy resource management systems, and we have applied the model to develop a system of social and institutional indicators.
the indicator system provides a framework for a more explicit consideration of the human dimensions of resource management.
the indicator system has utility in improving the management process by providing a framework to identify and measure the effects of management on the resource and the people who depend upon it.
The main takeaway from our work is that

social indicators can help to improve the management of natural resources by helping to identify the social dimensions of the resource system and to improve the quality of the management decision‐making process.
social and institutional dimensions should be given more explicit attention in wildlife and fishery management.
the social dimension should be explicitly considered as a management dimension, and that the social dimension is not a subset of the institutional dimension.
